content.title: About
content.content: Fish timbale (or fish mousse) is a delicate dish made from fish fillet, eggs, cream and aromatic herbs, baked in small individual molds. The texture can range from firm to airy depending on the recipe.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the French word “timbale”, meaning a baking mold.
It is often served cold as an appetizer at buffets and banquets.
Mousse versions are steamed, giving a lighter, more airy consistency.
Various fish can be used – from tender sea bass to richer salmon.
Traditionally the dish is garnished with micro‑greens, caviar or thin vegetable ribbons.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fish provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Timbale supplies all essential amino acids for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Fish is a source of selenium, iodine and phosphorus, essential for thyroid health and bones.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to fish and seafood.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination risk
items.content: Large predatory fish can contain mercury; choose smaller fish or trusted sources.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salty ingredients (e.g., soy sauce) can make the dish overly salty.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking may allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the timbale chilled, unmolded, garnished with micro‑greens, caviar, thin vegetable ribbons or a yogurt‑based sauce. It works well as bite‑size appetizers on a platter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the finished timbale in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a separate package for up to 1 month, thawing in the fridge before serving.
